noteBlocks.caption: Copy every chromosome, line the copies up across the middle, pull them apart: two cells, each with the parent's set.

noteBlocks.md: **Mitosis** is how a body cell makes two new cells. First the cell grows and **copies every chromosome exactly**. The copies line up across the middle of the cell, are pulled apart, and the cell divides **once**.

Each **daughter cell** gets one copy of every chromosome, so it has the **same number** of chromosomes and the **same genes** as the parent. Cells genetically identical to the cell they came from are **clones**. Growing, copying and dividing, again and again, is the **cell cycle**.

noteBlocks.stem: A body cell of a pea plant has 14 chromosomes. Describe what happens to them when the cell divides by mitosis, and what the new cells hold. [3]

steps.working: The cell copies all 14 chromosomes exactly.
steps.decision: Copying comes first, so that there is a full set for each new cell.

steps.working: The copies line up across the middle, are pulled apart, and the cell divides once.
steps.decision: One copy of each chromosome goes to each side, so neither cell can end up short of one.

steps.working: Two daughter cells, each with 14 chromosomes, genetically identical to the parent: clones.
steps.decision: Same number, same genes. Nothing was halved, because each cell received a whole set.

noteBlocks.prompt: A mouse body cell has 40 chromosomes and divides by mitosis. Which describes the new cells?
options: two cells, each with 40 chromosomes, identical to the parent
two cells, each with 20 chromosomes, identical to each other
four cells, each with 40 chromosomes, all different
noteBlocks.answer: two cells, each with 40 chromosomes, identical to the parent
noteBlocks.explain: Mitosis copies all 40 chromosomes first, then gives one copy of each to each side, as the pea cell's 14 did in the See it. So there are two cells, each with the full 40: clones of the parent.

optionNotes.option: two cells, each with 20 chromosomes, identical to each other
optionNotes.why: It tempts because a cell splits in two, but the copying came first, so each new cell still holds all 40.

optionNotes.option: four cells, each with 40 chromosomes, all different
optionNotes.why: Four different cells is what meiosis makes; mitosis divides once, giving two cells with the parent's genes.

noteBlocks.stem: Name the use of mitosis in each case. (a) A toddler's legs grow longer. (b) The lining of the stomach is renewed every few days. [2]

steps.working: (a) Growth.
steps.decision: More cells, each grown to full size, make a longer leg.

steps.working: (b) Replacing worn-out cells.
steps.decision: Nothing was damaged: old cells wear away and identical new ones take their place.

noteBlocks.prompt: After a burn, new skin cells grow over the damaged area. Which use of mitosis is this?
options: repairing damaged tissue
replacing worn-out cells
growth
noteBlocks.explain: The skin was damaged by the burn, and new cells made by mitosis fill the gap: that is repair. Replacing is for cells that wear out with no damage, as the stomach lining in the See it.

optionNotes.option: replacing worn-out cells
optionNotes.why: It tempts because new skin cells take the old ones' place, but these cells were damaged by the burn, not worn out.

optionNotes.option: growth
optionNotes.why: The body is not getting bigger here; the new cells only fill the damaged area back in.

twin.prompt: A child's arm bones lengthen year by year as she gets taller. Which use of mitosis is this?
options: growth
repairing damaged tissue
making gametes
twin.explain: Nothing is damaged or worn out: the bones gain cells and get longer, so this is growth.

optionNotes.option: repairing damaged tissue
optionNotes.why: Repair needs damage first; these bones are whole and simply getting longer.

optionNotes.option: making gametes
optionNotes.why: Gametes are made by meiosis in the testes and ovaries; mitosis never makes them.

noteBlocks.md: **Meiosis** makes **gametes**: sperm and ova. It happens only in the **testes** and the **ovaries**. The chromosomes are copied once, then the cell divides **twice**, so one cell becomes **four**.

Each gamete gets **one chromosome from every pair**, so it has **half** the parent's number. A cell like this is **haploid**. Meiosis is a **reduction division**, because it reduces the chromosome number. The four gametes are **genetically different** from the parent and from each other.

noteBlocks.stem: A cell in the testis of a dog has 78 chromosomes. Describe the cells meiosis makes from it. [4]

steps.working: Two divisions of the nucleus.
steps.decision: One more division than mitosis, which is what makes four cells instead of two.

steps.working: Four sperm cells from the one cell.
steps.decision: Each division doubles the cells: one, then two, then four.

steps.working: Each with 39 chromosomes, one from every pair: haploid.
steps.decision: Half of 78. A reduction division hands each gamete one member of each pair.

steps.working: All four genetically different.
steps.decision: Each holds a different mixture of the pairs, so no two sperm carry the same genes.

noteBlocks.prompt: A cell in a sheep's ovary has 54 chromosomes and divides by meiosis. Which describes the cells it makes?
options: four cells, each with 27 chromosomes, all genetically different
four cells, each with 54 chromosomes, all genetically different
two cells, each with 27 chromosomes, genetically identical
noteBlocks.answer: four cells, each with 27 chromosomes, all genetically different
noteBlocks.explain: Meiosis divides twice, so one cell gives four, and each gets one chromosome from every pair: half of 54 is 27. As with the dog's 78 in the See it, the four are genetically different.

optionNotes.option: four cells, each with 54 chromosomes, all genetically different
optionNotes.why: Four cells is right, but meiosis is a reduction division: each gamete holds half the parent's 54.

optionNotes.option: two cells, each with 27 chromosomes, genetically identical
optionNotes.why: Two identical cells is mitosis's outcome; meiosis divides twice and its four cells all differ.

twin.prompt: A cell in a goat's testis has 60 chromosomes and divides by meiosis. Which describes the cells it makes?
options: four cells, each with 30 chromosomes, all different
two cells, each with 60 chromosomes, all different
four cells, each with 30 chromosomes, all identical
twin.answer: four cells, each with 30 chromosomes, all different
twin.explain: Two divisions give four cells; each has one of every pair, half of 60, so 30; and each holds a different mixture, so they differ.

optionNotes.option: two cells, each with 60 chromosomes, all different
optionNotes.why: Two cells with the full 60 is a mitosis count; meiosis gives four cells with half the number each.

optionNotes.option: four cells, each with 30 chromosomes, all identical
optionNotes.why: The count is right, but meiosis shuffles the pairs, so the four sperm are genetically different.

noteBlocks.md: Fertilisation joins **two** gametes, one from each parent. Their chromosomes add together in the **zygote**, the first cell of the new organism.

noteBlocks.title: Why the number must halve
noteBlocks.md: If gametes kept the full number, every generation would have **double** the chromosomes of the one before. Halving at meiosis and adding at fertilisation cancel out, so the zygote is **diploid** again, with the parents' number, and mitosis keeps that number in every body cell.

noteBlocks.stem: A chimpanzee's body cells have 48 chromosomes. Use numbers to explain why its gametes must hold half that number. [3]

steps.working: Without halving: 48 + 48 = 96 in the zygote.
steps.decision: Fertilisation adds the two gametes' chromosomes together.

steps.working: The next generation: 96 + 96 = 192.
steps.decision: The number would double every generation, and no two generations would match.

steps.working: With halving: 24 + 24 = 48, the same as the parents.
steps.decision: Meiosis halves, fertilisation restores: the number stays at 48 in every generation.

noteBlocks.prompt: A pea plant's body cells have 14 chromosomes. If its gametes were not halved, how many chromosomes would a zygote have?
noteBlocks.explain: Fertilisation adds the two gametes' chromosomes: 14 + 14 = 28, double the parent's number. That is why meiosis halves, as the chimpanzee's 48 + 48 showed in the See it.

twin.prompt: A cabbage plant's body cells have 18 chromosomes. If its gametes were not halved, how many chromosomes would a zygote have?
twin.explain: Two unhalved gametes add to 18 + 18 = 36, double the parent's 18. Meiosis halves each gamete to 9, so 9 + 9 = 18.

noteBlocks.md: Body cells hold their chromosomes in **pairs**, one of each pair from each parent: they are **diploid**. Gametes hold **one chromosome from each pair**: they are **haploid**. Mitosis makes diploid cells; meiosis makes haploid ones.

The paper often gives statements to sort: true for mitosis only, for meiosis only, or for both. Test each against the facts: divisions, cells, chromosome number, alike or different. A few fit both: each is a type of cell division, and in each the chromosomes are copied before the cell divides.

noteBlocks.stem: Is each statement true for mitosis only, for meiosis only, or for both? (a) It produces four cells. (b) It produces diploid cells. [2]

steps.working: (a) Meiosis only.
steps.decision: Two divisions make four cells; mitosis makes two.

steps.working: (b) Mitosis only.
steps.decision: Diploid means in pairs. Mitosis keeps every pair; meiosis leaves one chromosome from each.

noteBlocks.prompt: A statement reads: the chromosomes are copied before the cell divides. Is it true for mitosis only, for meiosis only, or for both?
options: both
mitosis only
meiosis only
noteBlocks.explain: Both kinds of division copy the chromosomes before they divide. What differs is what happens next: mitosis divides once, meiosis twice. The See it sorted two statements that fit only one; this one fits both.

optionNotes.option: mitosis only
optionNotes.why: It tempts because mitosis is the copying division, but meiosis copies the chromosomes once before its two divisions too.

optionNotes.option: meiosis only
optionNotes.why: Copying is not what makes meiosis different; its two divisions and haploid cells are, and mitosis copies first as well.

twin.prompt: A statement reads: it produces gametes. Is it true for mitosis only, for meiosis only, or for both?
options: meiosis only
mitosis only
both
twin.explain: Gametes are made only by meiosis, in the testes and ovaries. Mitosis makes body cells for growth, replacement and repair.

optionNotes.option: mitosis only
optionNotes.why: Mitosis makes body cells; gametes need half the chromosomes, which only meiosis gives.

optionNotes.option: both
optionNotes.why: Mitosis never makes gametes: its cells keep every pair, and a gamete must hold one of each.

noteBlocks.md: **Higher tier.** Before the first division of meiosis, the chromosomes line up **in their pairs** across the middle of the cell. Which member of a pair faces which side is down to chance, and each pair lines up **independently** of every other pair.

This is **independent assortment**. It reassorts the chromosomes, so the gametes carry different mixtures of the parents' chromosomes. That is the source of **variation**, and when the paper asks what it does, the word variation is the mark.

noteBlocks.stem: A cell has a long pair and a short pair; in each pair one chromosome is shaded. Explain how meiosis can give gametes that differ. [2]

steps.working: Line-up 1: the shaded long and the shaded short face the same side.
steps.decision: The chromosomes on each side end up in gametes together.

steps.working: Line-up 2: the shaded long faces one side and the shaded short the other.
steps.decision: Neither line-up is more likely; chance decides, pair by pair.

steps.working: So the gametes carry different mixtures of shaded and clear chromosomes: the source of variation.
steps.decision: Different mixtures in the gametes mean different offspring.

mitosis produces two daughter cells, meiosis produces four

scheme.examinerNote: The commonest cap is a pair of swapped numbers: four cells given to mitosis, or two to meiosis. A second is the word identical used of meiosis. Both cost an indicative point and usually a band. Capital letters and full stops are part of the within-band judgement, and the word variation must actually appear for the last point to count.

hints: Take one feature at a time and say what each process does with it, rather than describing one process and then the other.
Comparative sentences earn more than two separate lists.
parts.workedSolution: Mitosis divides the nucleus once, while meiosis divides it twice. Mitosis therefore produces two daughter cells and meiosis produces four. The two cells produced by mitosis are genetically identical to the parent cell, so they are clones of it, whereas the four cells produced by meiosis are all genetically different from one another. Mitosis keeps the chromosome number the same, so a cell with 46 chromosomes gives cells with 46; meiosis halves it, so the same cell gives gametes with 23, and that is why meiosis is called a reduction division. The body uses mitosis for growth, for replacing worn-out cells and for repairing damaged tissue, and it happens all over the body. Meiosis happens only in the ovaries and the testes, where it makes gametes, and independent assortment shuffles the chromosomes so that the gametes differ, which is the source of variation.

commonErrors.feedback: The two processes have swapped their products. Mitosis makes genetically identical clones; meiosis makes four cells that all differ.

findTheMistake.stem:
Seán is asked: 'For each statement, say whether it is true for mitosis only, for meiosis only, or for both. [3]'
His answers:
studentWorking: it repairs the skin after a graze: mitosis only
the cells it produces are haploid: both
it is a kind of cell division: both
findTheMistake.whatWentWrong: Lines 1 and 3 are right, and each earns its mark. Line 2 gives haploid cells to both divisions. Haploid means one chromosome from each pair, so the number has been halved, and only meiosis does that. Mitosis copies every chromosome first, so both of its cells keep every pair.
correction: it repairs the skin after a graze: mitosis only
the cells it produces are haploid: meiosis only
it is a kind of cell division: both
findTheMistake.feedback: Two marks of the three. The check that settles it: haploid is half the chromosome number, and only one of the two divisions is a reduction division.

findTheMistake.stem:
Aoife is asked: 'A human body cell divides by mitosis. How many chromosomes are in each daughter cell? [1]'
Her working:
studentWorking: cell division always halves the chromosome number
findTheMistake.whatWentWrong: Line 1 is right. Line 2 is the rule for the wrong division: only meiosis halves the chromosome number, and only because it is making gametes. Mitosis duplicates the chromosomes exactly first, so both daughter cells end up with a full set.
correction: mitosis duplicates them exactly, then shares one full set to each daughter cell
findTheMistake.feedback: No marks, because the one mark here was the number. A quick check: if every division halved the number, a body cell would run out of chromosomes within a few days of growing.

findTheMistake.stem:
Conor is asked: 'Name the process in meiosis that produces variation, and say what it does. [2]'
His answer:
studentWorking: it swaps pieces between the chromosomes so the gametes differ
findTheMistake.whatWentWrong: The second line describes a real idea, but the first names a process the specification explicitly leaves out. CCEA asks for independent assortment: the chromosomes of each pair are dealt out to the new cells at random, so every gamete gets a different combination.
correction: the chromosomes of each pair are dealt out at random, so every gamete gets a different combination
findTheMistake.feedback: One mark of the two. Learn the two words on their own: independent assortment is named in the specification, and crossing over is named as not required.

findings.rule: Meiosis: four genetically different haploid nuclei; the shuffling is called independent assortment.

findings.asked: Draw the products of cell division, name what meiosis produces, and give the sex chromosomes in germ cells and in individual sperm.

findings.rule: Germ cells are diploid (XY); each sperm is haploid and carries X or Y.

insight.ruleToRemember: Mitosis makes two identical diploid cells (growth, replacing worn-out cells, repairing damaged tissue). Meiosis makes four genetically different haploid gametes with half the chromosome number; independent assortment is the source of the variation. Count chromosomes: 46 in body cells and germ cells, 23 in gametes.
